report.incident_title: API gateway p99 latency and 504s spiking
report.summary: Confirmed by metrics and traces: after the pdp_cache_include_reviews change (recorded 18:30Z, 0% to 100%, E51), product:pdp:* cache values grew from about 4.1 KB to about 38 KB (roughly 9x) between 18:30 and 18:55Z (E11, E42). Redis reached 100% of maxmemory by 19:05Z, evictions started at 19:05Z (about 5000/s by 19:10Z), and the hit ratio fell from 0.95 to about 0.40 (E9, E23, E10). The resulting cache-miss storm drove catalog-db CPU to 97-99% by 19:10Z (E12). catalog-svc then logged a DB pool wait over 2000 ms with 312 requests waiting (E13, E18), and catalog-svc p99 went from about 85 ms to 5000 ms (E4, E21). Gateway p99 rose to 5000 ms and 504s reached about 34% (E1, E2). A sampled trace shows gateway self-time of about 10 ms against a 4990 ms catalog-svc span, with a 4600 ms catalog-db review query (E29, E30). Gateway CPU stayed at 26-32% throughout (E3, E20), and there are no TLS or handshake errors (E8, E15, E16). Assumptions still open: the 18:30 flag state is taken from the change record and not confirmed by a config or flag source, catalog-db connection and query-latency data is missing, and the 17:40-18:00 metric gap means the 17:50 cipher change has no metric baseline. Scaling the gateway is not supported by the evidence, because gateway CPU is low and the gateway is waiting on catalog-svc.
report.root_cause: The pdp_cache_include_reviews flag change at 18:30Z (E51) made catalog-svc cache product:pdp entries with the latest 200 reviews embedded, raising cached PDP values from about 4.1 KB to about 38 KB (E11, E42). Redis hit maxmemory at 19:05Z, causing evictions and a hit-ratio collapse to about 0.40 (E9, E23, E10). The resulting cache-miss load, with reviews fetched from catalog-db, saturated catalog-db CPU and exhausted the catalog-svc DB pool (E12, E13, E18, E30). catalog-svc p99 then reached 5000 ms, and the gateway timed out upstream calls and returned 504s (E4, E2, E29). The flag cause rests on change-record and timing evidence and has not been confirmed from a flag-state source.

hypotheses.statement: The pdp_cache_include_reviews flag ramp at 18:30 increased PDP payload size ~9× (E11), causing Redis memory to saturate by 19:05 (E9/E22/E41), triggering evictions (E9/E23/E34) and cache‐miss storm (E17), which drove catalog-DB CPU to saturation by 19:10 (E12/E36) and exhausted catalog-svc DB pool (E13/E18). This caused catalog-svc p99 to jump to ~5s (E4/E21/E31/E46), leading to gateway upstream timeouts and 504s (E8/E2/E29).

corrective_actions.action: Roll back pdp_cache_include_reviews to 0% on catalog-svc now, then confirm the flag state from the flag system and watch Redis memory, eviction rate and catalog-db CPU recover. Do not scale the gateway as the primary response.
corrective_actions.rationale: The flag change is the earliest and only change that lines up with the payload growth, memory saturation and DB overload, and reverting it removes the source of the cache-miss storm without touching security controls.

corrective_actions.action: Redesign the PDP cache so reviews are not embedded in the product:pdp entry. Cache reviews under a separate key with its own size bound, or cap the number of embedded reviews, and test the payload size before re-enabling.
corrective_actions.rationale: Embedding 200 reviews multiplied the value size about 9x, which is the direct cause of the memory pressure.

corrective_actions.action: Gate flag ramps on cache-payload and Redis-memory headroom, and set a ramp rule that stops the rollout when avg value size or used_memory rises sharply. Add a capacity review for redis-cache maxmemory against the expected PDP working set.
corrective_actions.rationale: The 100% ramp was made without a check on how the cache would grow, and memory reached saturation about 35 minutes after the change.

corrective_actions.action: Add alerts on redis avg_value_size for product:pdp:*, on used_memory_pct above 85%, on eviction rate above zero, and on hit-ratio drops. Add catalog-db pool and query-latency metrics, and gateway connection-pool metrics, so H1-style causes can be tested directly.
corrective_actions.rationale: The first warning signs (payload growth from 18:30 and memory above 80% by 18:45) came well before the 19:12 page, and current gaps stopped the team from testing the other hypotheses.

catalog-svc latency_p99 was 84-86 ms from 18:00 to 18:25Z, 88 ms at 18:30Z, and rose gradually to 106 ms by 19:00Z. It then jumped to 900 ms at 19:05Z, 4200 ms at 19:10Z, and sat at about 5000 ms (apparently a ceiling) from 19:15Z to 19:35Z. The collapse coincides with the redis eviction and catalog-db saturation window.

Timing: the redis payload-size growth (18:30-18:35Z) and the catalog-db CPU drift (18:30-19:00Z) both start at the 18:30Z catalog flag change, before the 19:05Z cache-saturation step. This is consistent with the flag causing the memory pressure, which then drives the hit-ratio collapse and DB load. The data does not isolate the flag as the sole cause.

catalog-db CPU is not saturated before 19:05Z (max 45%), and catalog-svc p99 is nearly flat until 19:00Z. Neither service shows a degradation in the 17:50Z cipher-change window within my query range (18:00-20:00Z), which weakly argues against H2 as the primary driver of the catalog path. This is outside the scope of the cipher change itself, so it is not conclusive.

Nothing in these series points at api-gateway worker or connection-pool limits. The catalog-svc latency and redis/catalog-db saturation are downstream of the gateway, and the gateway CPU is reported normal. These series do not test H1 directly; api-gateway metrics were not queried.
